Interim data from HAL-CINP-203 analysis was released in December 2025 and top-line results are expected in November of 2026.

These clinical results are expected to provide important information regarding the future development and commercialization prospects of the IPR&D asset and may significantly impact management's estimates of future cash flows and fair value.

Events and circumstances that could result in a future impairment charge include, but are not limited to, (i) a sustained decline in the Company's stock price or market capitalization, including declines in average market capitalization measures over extended periods; (ii) increases in discount rates resulting from changes in market conditions, interest rates or company-specific risk factors; (iii) changes in assumptions regarding control premiums or other valuation inputs; (iv) adverse clinical trial results, including the anticipated fourth-quarter 2026 CINP data readout; (v) delays in, or failure to obtain, regulatory approval; (vi) unfavorable changes in projected cash flows, development costs or commercialization assumptions; and (vii) the emergence of competing therapies or changes in the standard of care for chemotherapy-induced neuropathic pain.

In December 2025, we announced interim results from a planned interim assessment of the ongoing Halneuron ® Phase 2b trial, the goal of which was to finalize the statistical methodology and the endpoint analysis to be used to determine Halneuron ® safety and effectiveness as a treatment for CINP.

Based on the recommendation of the independent statisticians conducting the assessment to slightly increase sample size from the planned 200, we chose to enroll 239 patients to maintain 80+% power, and will have top-line data from the trial available in November of 2026.
Following the interim analysis of HAL-CINP-203, a decision was made to add an open-label extension (“OLE”) option for patients who successfully completed the double-blinded study.

Events that could cause management to conclude that fair value has declined below carrying value, and that could result in a material impairment charge in a future period, include but are not limited to, (i) a sustained decline in the Company's stock price or market capitalization, including declines in average market capitalization measures over extended periods; (ii) increases in discount rates resulting from changes in market conditions, interest rates or company-specific risk factors; (iii) changes in assumptions regarding control premiums or other valuation inputs; (iv) adverse clinical trial results, including the anticipated fourth-quarter 2026 CINP data readout; (v) delays in, or failure to obtain, regulatory approval; (vi) unfavorable changes in projected cash flows, development costs or commercialization assumptions; and (vii) the emergence of competing therapies or changes in the standard of care for chemotherapy-induced neuropathic pain.
